dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: The target proposition asserts the existence of a real constant C at least 1 which works uniformly for every finite nonempty family of independent, integrable, centered, variance-one real random variables satisfying LocalDef003, every real coefficient family, and every real p at least 2, giving both the Euclidean lower bound and a subgaussian Lp upper bound for the weighted sum.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the complete logical and quantitative content of the proposition, including the order of the existential and universal quantifiers and both inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006

binders: There exists a real constant C.
Universally quantify over types iota and Omega, with iota finite and nonempty and Omega equipped with a measurable space.
Universally quantify over a probability measure mu on Omega and a family X = (X_i) indexed by iota of real-valued functions on Omega.
Universally quantify over every real coefficient family a = (a_i) and every real exponent p.
hypotheses: For every i, X_i is measurable and has some real K_i > 0 such that exp(X_i^2/K_i^2) is integrable and its mu-integral is at most 2.
For every i, X_i is integrable and integral_mu X_i = 0.
The indexed family (X_i) is jointly independent with respect to mu.
conclusions: ||sum_i a_i X_i||_{L^p(mu)} <= C * max_i ||X_i||_{psi_2} * sqrt(p) * sqrt(sum_i a_i^2), where the displayed family gauge is LocalDef004 with the precise infimum semantics below.
mathematical_definitions: For a real-valued X, its encoded psi_2 gauge is inf {t in [0,infinity] : t != 0, t != infinity, X is measurable, exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) is integrable, and integral exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) dmu <= 2}.
The family gauge is max_i of the real conversion of the encoded psi_2 gauge of X_i; the index type is nonempty, so this finite maximum is defined.
The weighted random sum is omega |-> sum_i a_i X_i(omega), and the coefficient Euclidean norm is sqrt(sum_i a_i^2).
lpNorm is a real-valued totalization of the Lp seminorm: it is eLpNorm converted to a real for an almost-everywhere strongly measurable function and is 0 otherwise.
The real p is passed to lpNorm via ENNReal.ofReal; since p >= 2, this agrees with its ordinary nonnegative embedding.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal real constant C at least 1 such that, for every finite nonempty family of jointly independent, integrable, mean-zero, variance-one real random variables on a probability space, if every variable satisfies the stated exponential-square subgaussian condition, then for every real coefficient vector a and every real p >= 2, the Lp norm of the weighted sum lies between the Euclidean norm of a and C times sqrt(p), the Euclidean norm of a, and the maximum encoded psi_2 gauge of the variables. The existential choice of C precedes and is independent of the probability space, family, coefficients, and p.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type must be finite and nonempty; the theorem says nothing directly about empty or infinite families.
Every variable is normalized to exact variance 1 and exact mean 0, so this is not stated for arbitrary variance scales or noncentered variables.
The same global constant C works uniformly and must satisfy C >= 1, but no optimality or explicit numerical value is asserted.
The exponent p is a real number constrained by p >= 2; the Lp exponent is ENNReal.ofReal p.
The local subgaussian predicate explicitly requires measurability and a positive finite real witness K with integrable exponential-square moment at most 2.

The gauge infimum separately ranges over nonzero, non-infinite ENNReal scales and does not itself state that the admissible set is nonempty; the subgaussian hypotheses are intended to supply finite admissible scales.

ENNReal.toReal and the real-valued variance and lpNorm definitions are totalized at exceptional values. In particular lpNorm is 0 for a function not almost-everywhere strongly measurable, though the hypotheses should make the finite weighted sum measurable.

The lower inequality is nontrivial only because centering, independence, and unit variance force the second moment of the weighted sum to match sum_i a_i^2; for the zero coefficient vector both bounds collapse to zero.
Independence is the indexed joint-independence predicate, not merely pairwise independence.
All equalities and inequalities are exact, with no almost-sure qualifications stated outside the measure-theoretic norm semantics.
ambiguities: The dossier exposes the kernel-based definition of indexed independence only one level deep; it clearly asserts joint indexed independence, but its full event-level expansion is outside the semantic frontier.
The internal proof argument establishing nonemptiness for Finset.sup' is elided, although the explicit Nonempty iota assumption and D065 determine its mathematical role.

The exact behavior of ENNReal.toReal at infinity is represented only through its toNNReal implementation in the dossier; exceptional-value totalization is therefore noted rather than used to simplify the main claim.
